jurisdiction.name: Latvia
jurisdiction.overview: Nationally published records appear separately from applicable EU-level records. The landscape, historical relationships and legal applicability remain under document-level review.

narrative.summary: Latvia combines the EU AI Act with a growing national layer: a 2020 Cabinet informative report on AI serves as its strategy, the 2025 AI Centre Law created a national AI Centre with a regulatory sandbox set out in a 2026 Cabinet regulation, and a 2025 law makes the central bank (Latvijas Banka) the AI Act supervisor for financial institutions while 2026 amendments give the Ombudsman AI Act fundamental-rights powers. 2024 amendments created a criminal offence for deepfakes and AI-labelling rules for election campaigning. The regional development and digital ministry (VARAM) leads public-sector AI, with 2025 practical guidelines for AI in public bodies, a government AI target architecture, education guidance and the national CERT's AI security advice.
lead_institutions: Ministry of Smart Administration and Regional Development (VARAM)
narrative.review_notes: This review was completed on 12 October 2026 and covers national law, government, ministries and regulators. The acts designating most AI Act market-surveillance authorities and setting penalties had not been found in force and are listed as leads.

instruments.official_title: Praktiskās vadlīnijas MI ieviešanai iestāžu darbā un pakalpojumos
instruments.english_title: Practical Guidelines for Implementing AI in the Work and Services of Public Bodies
instruments.issuing_authority: Ministry of Smart Administration and Regional Development (VARAM), prepared with the State School of Administration project 'Public Administration Digital Academy', with forewords by CERT.LV and the Data State Inspectorate
instruments.publisher_name: Ministry of Smart Administration and Regional Development
instruments.summary: Government-wide practical guidelines from VARAM setting a common, secure approach to AI use in Latvian public administration. They cover AI principles and the legal framework (incl. the EU AI Act), selecting and assessing tasks, an AI solution life-cycle methodology, choosing AI solutions and suppliers, and secure use in institutions, with 13 annexes including an institutional self-assessment, a risk/requirements decision tree, a whitelist approach to approved AI tools, staff 'do/don't' rules and a generative-AI reminder for employees. They are guidance for state and municipal bodies, not binding rules.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Central public-sector AI and generative-AI guidance for Latvian institutions.
instruments.current_status: Published on varam.gov.lv on 10.12.2025 (page updated 17.01.2026; PDF updated 11.02.2026). The 68-page PDF cover is dated October 2025. VARAM invites feedback for updates at MaksligaisIntelekts@varam.gov.lv.

instruments.official_title: Kārtība, kādā Mākslīgā intelekta centrs organizē speciālo regulatīvo vidi un datu apstrādi
instruments.english_title: Procedure by which the Artificial Intelligence Centre organises the special regulatory environment and data processing (Cabinet Regulation No. 12)
instruments.issuing_authority: Cabinet of Ministers (responsible institution: Ministry of Smart Administration and Regional Development)
instruments.summary: Cabinet Regulation No. 12 of 13 January 2026, issued under Articles 8(5) and 9(8) of the Artificial Intelligence Centre Law, sets the rules of the AI special regulatory environment (sandbox) run by the foundation 'Mākslīgā intelekta centrs'. It defines the competent institutions (sector authority, data provider, municipality for real-world testing), free services for project implementers (compliance consultations, expert advice, a Central Statistical Bureau secure environment for state-held personal data, real-world testing, data from state information systems), project selection by the Centre, and requirements for personal-data storage, transfer, deletion and technical and organisational safeguards.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Latvia's legal basis for its national AI sandbox.
instruments.current_status: In force since 16.01.2026 (adopted 13.01.2026, prot. No. 1 §40; Latvijas Vēstnesis No. 9, 15.01.2026, OP 2026/9.11). Record re-pointed from the VARAM press release of 14.01.2026 announcing the regulation to the regulation itself on likumi.lv.

instruments.issuing_authority: CERT.LV (Information Technology Security Incident Response Institution of the Republic of Latvia)
instruments.summary: CERT.LV security recommendations on using ChatGPT and other generative AI tools. It warns about malicious ads, fake AI apps and browser extensions, advises not to enter personal, sensitive or restricted information, to fact-check outputs and beware bias and copyright issues, and recommends that companies and organisations adopt internal rules and staff training for AI use rather than outright bans, or consider self-hosted language models.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: National cyber authority's generative-AI security advice.
instruments.current_status: Published 31.05.2023 on cert.lv (cert.gov.lv) as an alert/recommendation; no later revision noted.

instruments.summary: Establishes the foundation 'Mākslīgā intelekta centrs' (Artificial Intelligence Centre) to build an AI ecosystem and a legal framework for public-private-university cooperation, and sets its aims (including ethical, responsible and safe AI use respecting fundamental rights and AI risk mitigation), tasks, rights, structure and financing. Tasks include promoting AI uptake, identifying AI security risks, issuing opinions on AI or deepfake use in pre-election campaigning, elections and Saeima appointment processes (from 1 June 2026), guidance and consultations, Latvian-language datasets, and running a special regulatory environment (sandbox) with data-processing rules (Arts. 8-9). The Centre is supervised by VARAM for delegated tasks.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Founding law of Latvia's national AI body and legal basis of its AI sandbox.
instruments.current_status: In force since 20.03.2025 (adopted 06.03.2025; Latvijas Vēstnesis No. 55, 19.03.2025). Amended by the law of 14.05.2026 (LV No. 97, 22.05.2026; in force 01.06.2026) restructuring the Centre's governance (council and board/director). Implemented by Cabinet Regulation No. 12 of 13.01.2026.

instruments.official_title: Finanšu tirgus digitālās darbības noturības un mākslīgā intelekta izmantošanas likums
instruments.english_title: Law on Digital Operational Resilience and the Use of Artificial Intelligence in the Financial Market
instruments.summary: Applies the EU DORA Regulation (2022/2554) and the AI Act (Regulation 2024/1689) in the Latvian financial market. Article 7 applies the AI Act's AI-use requirements to the financial entities covered by the law, and Article 8 designates Latvijas Banka to supervise compliance with the AI-use requirements under Article 74(6) of the AI Act, share relevant findings with the ECB, and apply sanctions and administrative measures (Arts. 10-14).
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: National AI Act implementing law for the financial sector; designates the central bank as AI market surveillance authority for financial institutions.
instruments.current_status: In force since 01.10.2025 (adopted 11.09.2025; Latvijas Vēstnesis No. 188, 30.09.2025).

instruments.official_title: Grozījumi Krimināllikumā (2024. gada 26. septembra likums; 90.2 pants par dziļviltojuma tehnoloģijas izmantošanu)
instruments.english_title: Amendments to the Criminal Law (Law of 26 September 2024; Section 90.2 on use of deepfake technology)
instruments.summary: Adds Section 90.2 to the Criminal Law, criminalising the knowing production or dissemination, by means of deepfake technology, of false discrediting information about a candidate for a state office elected, appointed or approved by the Saeima during that process, punishable by up to five years' imprisonment or lesser penalties. The amending law (with related election-interference provisions) applies to deepfakes used to influence democratic processes.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Criminal offence targeting AI deepfakes in Saeima appointment processes.
instruments.current_status: In force since 22.10.2024 (adopted 26.09.2024; Latvijas Vēstnesis No. 196, 08.10.2024). The official title of the act is 'Grozījumi Krimināllikumā'; the parenthetical identifies this amending law.

instruments.official_title: Grozījumi Priekšvēlēšanu aģitācijas likumā (2024. gada 24. oktobra likums; 3.1 pants par mākslīgā intelekta sistēmu izmantošanu)
instruments.english_title: Amendments to the Pre-election Campaigning Law (Law of 24 October 2024; Section 3.1 on the use of AI systems)
instruments.summary: Adds Section 3.1 requiring that any AI-generated depiction of a person or of an unreal event (image, audio or video) used in paid pre-election campaigning or campaign material be clearly and unambiguously labelled, bans the use of automated systems for campaigning via fake or anonymous social-media accounts (Section 18(6)), and empowers the head of the Corruption Prevention and Combating Bureau (KNAB) to order a halt to further distribution of non-compliant AI-generated campaign material (Section 31.1).
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: AI labelling and deepfake rules for election campaigning.
instruments.current_status: In force since 07.11.2024 (adopted 24.10.2024; Latvijas Vēstnesis No. 217, 06.11.2024). The official title of the act is 'Grozījumi Priekšvēlēšanu aģitācijas likumā'; the parenthetical identifies this amending law.

instruments.english_title: Informative Report 'On the Development of Artificial Intelligence Solutions'
instruments.issuing_authority: Cabinet of Ministers (prepared by the Ministry of Environmental Protection and Regional Development, now VARAM)
instruments.summary: Latvia's first government policy document on AI, serving as its national AI strategy in response to the EU Coordinated Plan on AI. It describes the technology, its socio-economic effects, international and Latvian experience, education and research, data and computing capacity, risks and regulation, and sets further action directions for promoting AI in public administration and the economy over three years, naming VARAM as lead institution for AI in public administration and feeding AI actions into the Digital Transformation Guidelines 2021-2027.
instruments.current_status: Adopted by the Cabinet on 04.02.2020 (policy planning document, policy area: public administration). Not formally superseded; AI governance has since been developed through the Digital Transformation Guidelines 2021-2027, the 2025 AI Act implementation report and the AI Centre Law.

instruments.official_title: Informatīvais ziņojums "Par Mākslīgā intelekta akta prasību ieviešanu"
instruments.english_title: Informative Report 'On the Implementation of the Requirements of the Artificial Intelligence Act'
instruments.issuing_authority: Ministry of Smart Administration and Regional Development (considered by the Cabinet of Ministers on 25 February 2025, protocol No. 8)
instruments.publisher_name: Ministry of Smart Administration and Regional Development
instruments.summary: Sets Latvia's institutional plan for the EU AI Act: VARAM as overall responsible authority and contact with the Commission, the Ministry of Economics as notifying authority, the Latvian National Accreditation Bureau as accreditation body, the Ombudsman as fundamental-rights authority, and a set of sectoral market surveillance authorities (incl. the Consumer Rights Protection Centre, Health Inspectorate, State Data Inspectorate for prohibited practices and high-risk systems, and Latvijas Banka for financial institutions). Its annexes list required legislative amendments, the division of responsibilities, resources and the national AI regulatory sandbox; the Cabinet instructed all ministries to review their legislation by 1 May 2025.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Latvia's AI Act governance and authority-designation plan.
instruments.current_status: Considered by the Cabinet on 25.02.2025 (protocol No. 8, para. 14 instructed ministries to assess and prepare amendments by 01.05.2025). Designations are being implemented through sectoral laws (e.g. the 2025 financial-market law); no single horizontal AI Act implementation law was found in force as of 12.10.2026.

instruments.official_title: Grozījumi Tiesībsarga likumā (2026. gada 15. janvāra likums; tiesībsarga pilnvaras mākslīgā intelekta sistēmu jomā)
instruments.english_title: Amendments to the Ombudsman Law (Law of 15 January 2026; Ombudsman powers concerning AI systems)
instruments.summary: Implements the Ombudsman's role as fundamental-rights authority under the EU AI Act by adding Section 13(15)-(16) to the Ombudsman Law: the Ombudsman may request and access AI system documentation needed in an investigation case and may submit a reasoned request to the competent market surveillance authority to organise technical testing of an AI system where the documentation is insufficient. Section 27(1) is amended so the Ombudsman sets the scope and deadline for such information requests.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: National AI Act implementation: fundamental-rights authority powers (AI Act Art. 77).
instruments.current_status: In force since 11.02.2026 (adopted 15.01.2026; Latvijas Vēstnesis No. 19, 28.01.2026, OP 2026/19.2). The official title of the act is 'Grozījumi Tiesībsarga likumā'; the parenthetical identifies this amending law.

coverage_audit.no_material_found_note: Latvia's legislation portal, parliament, Cabinet, ministries and regulators were searched. No horizontal law implementing the AI Act and no pending AI bill was found, and there was no material for standards, indices, drafts, international instruments or older publications. The utilities regulator and the health regulators were not searched separately, and the data inspectorate's standalone AI guidance, the date of a defence ministry report and the national adoption of an AI standard remain to be checked.
